description: group_j._HUMAN_TOUCH_PATTERNS line 60: '(re.compile(r"[\"\']escalation[\"\']"), "gh-issue-escalation")' — matches the literal substring 'escalation' ONLY when surrounded by quote marks. But REQ-F1 step 6 bans any gh issue label containing the substring 'escalation' (not just quoted). 'gh issue create --label escalation' (unquoted in shell) or 'subprocess.run(["gh", "issue", "create", "--label", "escalation"])' inside a list literal does contain quotes around the word — these match. But a python f-string like f'gh issue create --label {label}' where label = 'escalation' would NOT be caught at static analysis time. Other patterns use \b word-boundary (e.g. \bneeds-login\b) which would catch un-quoted forms. Inconsistent pattern strictness leaves a small-but-real bypass.

evidence.snippet: (re.compile(r"['\"]escalation['\"]"), "gh-issue-escalation")  # only matches quoted; \bescalation\b would be consistent with sibling patterns
